app.name: NonvisualAudio
status.done: Analysis complete. Results are in the results window.
status.partial: Analysis complete. Some files could not be processed.
ui.main.title: NonvisualAudio
ui.main.intro:
Pick one or more audio files to analyze. Optionally choose
one or more genre references, a reference file, or both.
Press "Analyze" to run. The report opens in a separate window.
ui.hint.open_file: Select the audio file you want to analyze.
ui.hint.clear_files: Remove all files from the list so you can start fresh.
ui.hint.targets_view: Read-only list of audio files that will be analyzed. Drop files or folders here, or press Command V or Control V to paste copied paths. Each file produces its own section in the report. Use Clear Files to start over.
ui.clipboard_scan.title: Import audio files from clipboard?
ui.clipboard_scan.body.one: 1 audio file was found on the clipboard. Add it to the analysis list?
ui.clipboard_scan.body.other: {count} audio files were found on the clipboard. Add them to the analysis list?
ui.hint.genre_picker: Choose a genre to compare the file against.
ui.hint.selected_genres: Which genre references the report will compare against. Use the Choose Genres button to change this selection.
ui.hint.reference_file: Select one or more audio files (or drop a folder onto the reference area) to use as the comparison reference. Multiple files are combined into a reference project that is matched against your target as a whole.
ui.hint.clear_reference: Remove the currently selected reference so the report does not include a reference comparison.
ui.hint.selected_reference: Which audio the report will use as a reference comparison. A single file is compared one-to-one; several files are combined into a reference project. Use the Choose Reference Files button to change the selection, or drop files / a folder here.
ui.hint.analyze: Run the analysis and display results in a separate window.
ui.hint.progress_bar: Progress of the running analysis, from zero to one hundred percent.
ui.hint.progress_stage: Live status of the running analysis. Reads the current stage and percentage complete.
ui.hint.results: The full text report. Read line by line with your screen reader. Press Control C or Command C to copy.
ui.hint.copy_results: Copy the full report text to the clipboard so you can paste it elsewhere.
ui.hint.sections_picker: Choose which sections appear in the report — for example only loudness and dynamics, or only frequency balance. Default is every section.
ui.hint.selected_sections: Which sections the report will include. Use the Choose Report Sections button to change this.
ui.hint.project_mode: When enabled, all selected files are treated as one continuous project. Loudness, dynamics, and frequency balance are measured across the whole set as if it were a single file, and a cross-track consistency block is added. In project mode the clipping display behaves differently than in single-file analysis: the timestamp of the loudest true peak is omitted, because the measurement runs across the combined project timeline and cannot be tied to a single file.
ui.project_mode.single_file.title: Project mode with only one file
ui.project_mode.single_file.body:
Project mode combines several tracks into a single analysis, but only one file is in the list — there is nothing to combine.

Yes: switch project mode off and run a normal single-file analysis (recommended).
No: keep project mode on and run a one-track project anyway.
Cancel: go back and add more files first.
ui.placeholder.no_files: No audio files selected. Click Add Audio Files to choose one or more.
ui.placeholder.no_genres: No genres selected. Standalone analysis will be used. Click Choose Genres to add one or more.
ui.placeholder.no_reference: No reference selected. Click Choose Reference Files to pick one or several, or drop a folder here.
ui.placeholder.no_sections: No report sections selected. The report will be empty. Click Choose Report Sections to pick one or more.
ui.list.sections_all: All report sections will be included.
ui.menu.genre_editor.hint: Add, edit, delete, or reset genre reference profiles.
ui.menu.about.hint: Show version, credits, README, and a link to file a bug report.
ui.menu.diagnostics.hint: Create a support report with system information and recent logs.
ui.menu.language.auto.hint: Follow the system locale. Clears any saved language override.
ui.menu.theme.hint: Pick the colour scheme: follow the system, light, dark, or high contrast.
ui.menu.theme.auto.hint: Follow the operating system's light or dark mode.
ui.menu.theme.high_contrast.hint: Black background, saturated yellow text for maximum contrast.
ui.genre_picker.title: Choose genre references
ui.genre_picker.help: A list of genre profiles grouped by category. Tab between profiles and press Space to toggle each one. Any number of profiles can be selected at once.
ui.genre_picker.intro:
Pick one or more genres whose typical loudness and dynamics
you want the file compared against. You can select as many as
you like — the report will include a comparison for each.
ui.sections.title: Choose report sections
ui.sections.help: List of report sections. Tab between them and press Space to toggle each one. Disabled sections are skipped in the rendered report.
ui.sections.intro:
Pick the sections that should appear in the report.
Disabled sections are simply skipped — the rest keeps its
usual order so the report stays predictable.
ui.sections.hint.loudness: Integrated LUFS, short-term peak, true peak, loudness range.
ui.sections.hint.dynamics: Crest factor and dynamic range score.
ui.sections.hint.frequency: Energy per band and the prominent spectral peaks.
ui.sections.hint.overall: One-paragraph summary across loudness, dynamics, and tonal balance.
ui.sections.hint.comparison: Comparison sections against the chosen genre profiles or reference file. Auto-skipped when nothing is selected.
ui.sections.hint.recommendations: Actionable EQ and limiter suggestions derived from the measurements.
ui.results.title: Analysis Results — NonvisualAudio
ui.results.help: The full analysis report. Press Control Shift C or Command Shift C to copy. Press Escape to close and return to the main window.
ui.results.close_hint: Close this window and return to the main NonvisualAudio window.
ui.error_dialog.body_hint: Read through the explanation and the suggested next step, then close the dialog.
ui.genre_editor.title: Edit Genre Profiles
ui.genre_editor.name: Genre profile editor
ui.genre_editor.help: Add, edit, delete, or reset genre profiles. User-added entries and modifications are stored in the user data folder.
ui.genre_editor.intro:
Each line starts with the origin tag: built-in is a stock
profile, user is one you added, modified is a stock profile
you overrode. Delete removes user profiles; Reset restores a
modified built-in to its stock values.
ui.genre_editor.list_hint: List of all genre profiles. Use the up and down arrows to move through the list, then press Enter to edit the highlighted profile.
ui.genre_editor.filter_hint: Restrict the list to all profiles, only built-ins, only your own, or only built-ins you have modified.
ui.genre_editor.add_hint: Opens the form to create a brand new genre profile.
ui.genre_editor.edit_hint: Opens the edit dialog for the currently selected profile.
ui.genre_editor.reset_hint: Removes your changes to a built-in profile, restoring the stock values.
ui.genre_editor.close_hint: Close this window and go back to the main NonvisualAudio window.
ui.genre_editor.delete_prompt: Delete profile '{key}'? This cannot be undone.
ui.genre_editor.duplicate_key: A profile with key '{key}' already exists.
ui.genre_form.intro_add: Fill in the fields and press OK. Key and display name are required.
ui.genre_form.intro_edit: Update the fields and press OK to save.
ui.genre_form.field.key.name: Profile key
ui.genre_form.field.key.hint: Short internal identifier, lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. Auto-generated from the display name if you leave it empty. Cannot be changed after creation.
ui.genre_form.field.category.name: Category
ui.genre_form.field.category.hint: Pick an existing category from the popup menu. To create a new one, type its name into the 'or new category name' field below — it overrides this dropdown when filled.
ui.genre_form.field.new_category.name: New category name
ui.genre_form.field.new_category.hint: Type a brand-new category name here to create a new group in the genre picker. Leave empty to use the existing category selected above.
ui.genre_form.field.display_name_en.name: Display name in English
ui.genre_form.field.display_name_de.name: Display name in German
ui.genre_form.field.display_name.hint: The human-readable title shown in the genre picker and in the report. Fill in at least one language; the other can stay empty.
ui.genre_form.field.target_lufs.name: Target integrated loudness in LUFS
ui.genre_form.field.target_lufs.hint: Typical loudness value for this genre, for example minus 14 for streaming pop.
ui.genre_form.field.lra_low.name: Loudness range lower bound in LU
ui.genre_form.field.lra_low.hint: Smallest loudness range typical for this genre, for example 5 LU.
ui.genre_form.field.lra_high.name: Loudness range upper bound in LU
ui.genre_form.field.lra_high.hint: Largest loudness range typical for this genre. Must be greater than or equal to the lower bound.
ui.genre_form.field.notes_en.name: Notes in English
ui.genre_form.field.notes_de.name: Notes in German
ui.genre_form.field.notes.hint: Short plain-text description of the tonal character, shown in the comparison section of the report. Fill in at least one language.
ui.genre_form.error.display_name_require: At least one display name (English or German) is required.
ui.menu.language.restart_body: The new language will be used the next time you launch NonvisualAudio.
ui.genre_form.error.bad_key: The key must contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. Example: my_custom_genre.
ui.genre_form.error.field_not_number: {field} must be a number, for example -14 or 7.5.
ui.genre_form.error.lra_order: LRA low must be less than or equal to LRA high.
ui.genre_form.error.lra_negative: Loudness range values cannot be negative.
ui.about.title: About NonvisualAudio
ui.about.help: App information, README, and a shortcut to file a bug report. Tab between the buttons; press Escape to close.
ui.about.description: An accessible audio analyzer for blind and low-vision audio professionals. Reports loudness, dynamics, and frequency balance as a cleanly structured plain-text report that works with VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, and Orca. Everything runs locally — no cloud, no telemetry, no network calls.
ui.about.license_fallback: MIT License. See the LICENSE file in the project repository for the full text.
ui.about.info_hint: Description, copyright, website, and credits. Read line by line with your screen reader.
ui.about.readme_hint: Open the bundled user guide in your default browser. The page is shown in the currently selected interface language.
ui.about.report_bug_hint: Open the project's issue tracker on GitHub in your default browser so you can file a bug report.
ui.about.diagnostics_hint: Save a support report with system information and recent logs into the log folder. Use this when filing a bug report.
ui.about.close_hint: Close this window and return to the main NonvisualAudio window.
ui.about.readme_missing.title: Help page missing
ui.about.readme_missing.body: NonvisualAudio could not locate the bundled help page. This usually means the resources folder was not copied into the packaged app. The same content is also available on the project's GitHub page (linked above in the app information).
ui.diagnostics.title: Diagnostic Report
ui.diagnostics.help: Save a support report and choose how detailed the logs are. Tab between the controls; press Escape to close.
ui.diagnostics.description: NonvisualAudio keeps a log of what the app does and of any crashes. You can save that log as a diagnostic report and send it to the developer when you ask for support.
ui.diagnostics.privacy: Privacy: by default the report contains no full file paths and no user name — only file names. Enable verbose logging below only if the developer asks you to; it records full paths from that point on and helps track down path-related problems.
ui.diagnostics.info_hint: Explains what the report contains and how your privacy is protected. Read line by line with your screen reader.
ui.diagnostics.verbose_hint: When checked, new log entries include full file paths and the user name. Leave unchecked unless support asks for it. The setting is remembered between sessions.
ui.diagnostics.save_hint: Write the diagnostic report into the log folder, ready to attach to a support request.
ui.diagnostics.folder_hint: Open the folder that holds the log files in your file manager.
ui.diagnostics.close_hint: Close this window and return to the main NonvisualAudio window.
ui.diagnostics.save_ok.title: Report saved
ui.diagnostics.save_ok.body: The diagnostic report was saved as {filename} in the log folder. Use 'Open Log Folder' to find it and attach it to your support request.
ui.diagnostics.save_failed.title: Could not save report
ui.diagnostics.save_failed.body: NonvisualAudio could not write the diagnostic report into the log folder. Check that the folder is writable and try again.
ui.diagnostics.folder_failed.title: Could not open folder
ui.diagnostics.folder_failed.body: NonvisualAudio could not open the log folder. You can still save the report with the other button.
worker.error.no_files.title: No files to analyze
worker.error.no_files.body: No audio files are currently in the list.
worker.error.no_files.hint: Add at least one audio file, then press Analyze again.
worker.error.bad_reference.title: Reference file could not be analyzed
worker.error.bad_reference.extra_hint: You can also clear the reference file to run the analysis without one.
worker.error.unexpected.title: Unexpected error while analyzing {filename}
worker.error.unexpected.body: The audio pipeline raised an unexpected error.
worker.error.unexpected.hint: Try re-exporting the file as WAV or FLAC. If the problem persists, relaunch the app with NVA_DEBUG=1 to capture a detailed log.
worker.error.report_format.title: Could not format the report for {filename}
worker.error.report_format.hint: The underlying analysis succeeded; please try again.
worker.error.all_failed.title: None of the {count} files could be analyzed
worker.error.all_failed.body: Each file failed for a different reason. Open the Details button to see them all.
error.ffmpeg.missing.title: FFmpeg is missing
error.ffmpeg.missing.body: NonvisualAudio needs the ffmpeg audio engine to decode files and to measure loudness. The bundled copy could not be found and there is no ffmpeg on your system either.
error.ffmpeg.install.darwin: Install ffmpeg with Homebrew by running: brew install ffmpeg. Alternatively, download a static build from evermeet.cx and place the ffmpeg binary in your PATH.
error.ffmpeg.install.windows: Download ffmpeg from ffmpeg.org or install it with winget (winget install Gyan.FFmpeg) and make sure the ffmpeg.exe is reachable from your command prompt.
error.ffmpeg.install.linux: Install ffmpeg with your package manager, for example sudo apt install ffmpeg or sudo dnf install ffmpeg.
error.decoder.timeout.title: Reading {name} took too long
error.decoder.timeout.body: The audio engine did not finish decoding this file within the allowed time. The file may be extremely long, corrupt, or stored on a slow drive.
error.decoder.timeout.hint: Try copying the file to your local disk first, or trim it to a shorter segment.
error.decoder.engine.title: Audio engine could not be started
error.decoder.engine.body: FFmpeg is installed on the system path but the operating system refused to launch it for decoding this file.
error.decoder.engine.hint: Quit NonvisualAudio, reinstall ffmpeg, and open the app again. If the problem persists, run NonvisualAudio from a terminal with NVA_DEBUG=1 set to see the exact error.
error.decoder.generic.title: Could not decode {name}
error.decoder.generic.body: The audio engine rejected this file. It may be corrupt, encrypted (for example a DRM-protected iTunes purchase), or in a format this ffmpeg build does not support.
error.decoder.generic.hint.tail: Try re-exporting the file as WAV or FLAC from your editor. Technical detail from ffmpeg: {tail}
error.decoder.generic.hint.no_tail: Try re-exporting the file as WAV or FLAC from your editor.
error.decoder.empty_output.title: {name} contains no audio
error.decoder.empty_output.body: The audio engine opened the file but produced no samples. It may be an empty recording, a data-only container, or a video file without an audio track.
error.decoder.empty_output.hint: Pick a different file, or check the export settings that produced this one.
error.decoder.missing.title: {name} is not on disk anymore
error.decoder.missing.body: The file you picked could not be found at the original location. It was probably moved, renamed, or deleted after you added it to the list.
error.decoder.missing.hint: Clear the file list and add the audio file again.
error.decoder.not_file.title: {name} is not a regular file
error.decoder.not_file.body: The chosen path points to a folder, a device, or some other non-file object instead of an audio file.
error.decoder.not_file.hint: Pick an actual audio file such as a WAV, MP3, FLAC, or M4A.
error.decoder.empty.title: {name} is empty
error.decoder.empty.body: The file has a size of zero bytes and cannot be decoded.
error.decoder.empty.hint: Re-export or re-download the file, then try again.
error.decoder.unreadable.title: Cannot read {name}
error.decoder.unreadable.body: The operating system refused to read this file. Permissions may be restricted, or the drive may have disconnected. Details: {details}.
error.decoder.unreadable.hint: Check that you have read access to the file and that the drive is available.
error.loudness.no_summary.title: Loudness measurement failed for {name}
error.loudness.no_summary.body: The audio engine finished, but did not emit the EBU R128 summary that NonvisualAudio reads the numbers from. The file may be silent or extremely short.
error.loudness.no_summary.hint: Check that the file is longer than a few seconds and actually contains audible audio.
error.loudness.incomplete.title: Could not read loudness numbers for {name}
error.loudness.incomplete.body: The audio engine produced a summary but NonvisualAudio could not find one of the expected loudness values in it. This usually points to a non-standard or partial audio file.
error.loudness.incomplete.hint: Re-export the file as WAV or FLAC from your editor and try again.
error.loudness.timeout.title: Loudness scan of {name} took too long
error.loudness.timeout.body: The audio engine did not finish the EBU R128 loudness scan within the allowed time. The file may be extremely long or stored on a slow drive.
error.loudness.timeout.hint: Copy the file to a local drive or trim it to a shorter segment.
error.loudness.generic.title: Loudness measurement failed for {name}
error.loudness.generic.body: The audio engine exited with an error during the loudness scan. The file may be corrupt or in a format this ffmpeg build does not fully support.
error.loudness.generic.hint: Re-export the file as WAV or FLAC and try again.
error.app.crashed.title: Something went wrong inside NonvisualAudio
error.app.crashed.body:
The app hit an unexpected problem and recovered. Your selections were not lost, and you can try again.

Technical detail: {detail}
error.app.crashed.hint: If this keeps happening, relaunch NonvisualAudio from a terminal with NVA_DEBUG=1 set — that writes a detailed log to the terminal so the problem can be diagnosed.
report.loudness.verdict.very_loud: The file is very loud and likely heavily limited.
report.loudness.verdict.loud: The file is loud, consistent with modern streaming masters.
report.loudness.verdict.moderate: The file sits at a moderate loudness level typical of broadcast material.
report.loudness.verdict.quiet: The file is quiet, leaving plenty of headroom.
report.loudness.verdict.very_loud.projec: The project is very loud overall and likely heavily limited.
report.loudness.verdict.loud.project: The project is loud overall, consistent with modern streaming masters.
report.loudness.verdict.moderate.project: The project sits at a moderate loudness level typical of broadcast material.
report.loudness.verdict.quiet.project: The project is quiet overall, leaving plenty of headroom.
report.loudness.true_peak.risk: True peak is at or above minus 0.5 dBTP, which risks intersample clipping on lossy playback.
report.loudness.true_peak.close: True peak is close to full scale.
report.dynamics.verdict.compressed: Dynamics are highly compressed with very little headroom between peaks and average level.
report.dynamics.verdict.moderate: Dynamics are moderate, consistent with pop or broadcast mastering.
report.dynamics.verdict.wide: The file has a wide, healthy dynamic range.
report.dynamics.verdict.wide.project: The project has a wide, healthy dynamic range across all tracks.
report.freq.loudest_anchor: The loudest band in this file is the {name} region ({range}).
report.freq.loudest_anchor.project: Across the project, the loudest band is the {name} region ({range}).
report.freq.band_same_level: The {name} region ({range}) is roughly at the same level.
report.freq.quietest_suffix: — the quietest band in this file
report.freq.quietest_suffix.project: — the quietest band across the project
report.freq.spread_flat: Overall the six bands sit within {spread} dB of each other — a flat, even tonal balance.
report.freq.spread_total: Total spread between loudest ({loudest}) and quietest ({quietest}) band: {spread} dB.
report.freq.peak_line: Peak {index}: {hz} ({region}), about {prominence} dB above the surrounding spectrum. Typically perceived as {character}.
report.freq.no_peaks: No narrow resonances stand out above the surrounding spectrum.
report.peak_char.boxiness: boxiness or a honky, boxy character
report.peak_char.bite: bite, edge, or harshness on vocals
report.overall.loud_compressed: This is a loud, compressed master with little remaining headroom
report.overall.dynamic: This is a dynamic recording with natural peaks
report.overall.moderate: This file sits in a moderate loudness and dynamics range
report.overall.loud_compressed.project: Overall the project is loud and compressed with little remaining headroom
report.overall.dynamic.project: Overall the project is dynamic with natural peaks
report.overall.moderate.project: Overall the project sits in a moderate loudness and dynamics range
report.tonal.flat: with a flat tonal balance across all six bands
report.tonal.mild_lean: with a mild lean toward the {name} (about {spread} dB louder than the {quietest})
report.tonal.heavy: with a clearly {name}-heavy tonal balance — the {name} is {spread} dB louder than the {quietest}
report.rec.true_peak: Lower the true peak ceiling to minus 1 dBTP to prevent intersample clipping. In most brickwall limiters this is the Ceiling or Output Level parameter.
report.rec.limit_less: Consider reducing limiting to restore some dynamic range if the target platform allows it.
report.rec.air_boost: A small shelf boost of about 2 dB above 8 kHz can add clarity and air.
report.rec.sub_absent: The very low end is almost absent. If this is music, check whether the high pass filter on the mix or master bus is set too high.
report.rec.sub_dominant: The sub bass is dominant. A gentle reduction below 60 Hz with a high pass filter or a low shelf of about 2 dB usually improves overall mix clarity.
report.rec.none: No specific corrective actions are obvious from the measurements. The file appears balanced and well prepared.
report.rec.none.project: No specific corrective actions are obvious from the measurements. The project appears balanced and well prepared across all tracks.
report.peak_fix.rumble: The peak at {hz} is in the rumble and sub-sonic range, often caused by traffic, HVAC noise, footsteps, or DC offset. A high pass filter at about {hpf} Hz with a 12 dB per octave slope is usually more transparent than a notch cut. Listen for unwanted thinning of the bass when you set the cutoff.
report.peak_fix.mains: The peak at {hz} sits on the mains hum frequency. Start with a narrow notch, Q about 8, cutting around {cut} dB at exactly {hz}. If the peak is a musical note rather than a constant hum, widen the Q to about 3.
report.peak_fix.low_bass: For the low bass buildup at {hz}, start with a cut of about {cut} dB at that frequency, Q around 1.5 (roughly an octave wide). That typically tightens the low end without thinning the kick or bass.
report.peak_fix.muddiness: To reduce muddiness at {hz}, try a cut of about {cut} dB at that frequency with a medium Q of about 1.5. A/B the change on vocal and bass passages to avoid losing warmth.
report.peak_fix.low_mid: For the low midrange peak at {hz}, start with a cut of about {cut} dB, Q around 1.2, to open up the midrange and reduce boxiness without thinning the bass.
report.peak_fix.hollow: The peak at {hz} is in the hollow, cardboard range. A cut of about {cut} dB with Q around 1.5 is a safe starting point. If it is room resonance, the same EQ will help most material recorded in that room.
report.peak_fix.nasal: To tame the nasal or telephone-like quality at {hz}, try a cut of about {cut} dB with Q around 1.5. This region is very audible, so make small changes and compare often.
report.peak_fix.bite: For the bite or harshness at {hz}, start with a cut of about {cut} dB, Q around 1.5. On vocals a dynamic EQ often works better than a static cut, because this range only gets harsh on the loudest syllables.
report.peak_fix.sibilance: For the sibilance near {hz}, a narrow notch with Q about 3 and a cut of around {cut} dB is a good starting point. On vocal material a de-esser tuned to this frequency is usually cleaner than a static EQ cut.
report.peak_fix.upper_sibilance: The peak at {hz} is in the upper sibilance and air range. Try a cut of about {cut} dB, Q around 3, or a de-esser tuned to this frequency if it is a vocal problem.
report.peak_fix.brightness: For the brightness peak at {hz}, a high shelf starting one octave below, pulled down by about {cut} dB, usually sounds more natural than a narrow cut at the exact frequency.
report.comp.lufs_louder: At {target} LUFS, this file is about {diff} LU louder than {label}, which usually sits around {reference} LUFS. That means less dynamic headroom than the target expects.
report.comp.lufs_quieter: At {target} LUFS, this file is about {diff} LU quieter than {label}, which usually sits around {reference} LUFS.
report.comp.lufs_inline: At {target} LUFS, this file is in line with {label} (around {reference} LUFS).
report.comp.lufs_louder.project: At {target} LUFS, this project is about {diff} LU louder than {label}, which usually sits around {reference} LUFS. That means less dynamic headroom than the target expects.
report.comp.lufs_quieter.project: At {target} LUFS, this project is about {diff} LU quieter than {label}, which usually sits around {reference} LUFS.
report.comp.lufs_inline.project: At {target} LUFS, this project is in line with {label} (around {reference} LUFS).
report.comp.lra_narrow: The loudness range of {lra} LU is narrower than the {low} to {high} LU typical for this genre, suggesting heavier compression than expected.
report.comp.lra_wide: The loudness range of {lra} LU is wider than the {low} to {high} LU typical for this genre.
report.comp.lra_within: The loudness range of {lra} LU is within the typical {low} to {high} LU range for this genre.
report.comp.genre_notes: Typical tonal character for this genre: {notes}.
report.ref.loudness_diff: The target is about {diff} LU {direction} than the reference. Target integrated loudness is {target} LUFS, reference is {reference} LUFS.
report.ref.loudness_same: Target and reference integrated loudness are essentially the same.
report.ref.loudness_diff.project: The project is about {diff} LU {direction} than the reference. Project integrated loudness is {target} LUFS, reference is {reference} LUFS.
report.ref.loudness_same.project: Project and reference integrated loudness are essentially the same.
report.ref.lra_diff: The target has a {direction} loudness range than the reference by about {diff} LU.
report.ref.lra_diff.project: The project has a {direction} loudness range than the reference by about {diff} LU.
report.ref.dyn_diff: The target is {direction} than the reference by about {diff} dB of crest factor.
report.ref.dyn_diff.project: The project is {direction} than the reference by about {diff} dB of crest factor.
report.ref.band_diff: The {name} region is about {diff} dB {direction} than the reference.
report.ref.freq_same: The frequency balance is very similar to the reference.
report.project.name: Project name: {name}.
report.project.loudness_consistent: Per-track integrated loudness varies by less than {spread} LU — the project plays back at a consistent level.
report.project.loudness_spread: Per-track integrated loudness varies by {spread} LU. Loudest: {loudest_name} at {loudest_value} LUFS. Quietest: {quietest_name} at {quietest_value} LUFS.
report.project.no_consistency_findings: Not enough data to compare tracks against each other.
worker.error.project_failed.title: Project analysis could not finish
worker.error.project_failed.body: The whole-project pipeline raised an unexpected error.
worker.error.project_failed.hint: Try analyzing the files individually first to find the one that breaks the project pass.
